overall_assessment: The codebase has critical security and functional issues that prevent it from meeting the PRD and architectural requirements. The authentication system is fundamentally broken due to improper JWT handling and password hashing, and key features like user scoping and input validation are missing. Multiple critical bugs must be fixed before the system can be considered viable.

bugs.description: Password is not being hashed before storage. The signup endpoint directly saves the plain text password to the database, creating a severe security vulnerability.
bugs.suggested_fix: Use bcrypt or similar library to hash the password before saving. Example: password_hash = bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode('utf-8'), bcrypt.gensalt())

bugs.description: JWT token is returned in plain text without secure cookie settings. This exposes the application to XSS and CSRF attacks.
bugs.suggested_fix: Return JWT in a secure, httpOnly cookie with SameSite=Strict attribute instead of JSON body.

bugs.description: Expense creation endpoint does not validate category against predefined list. Users can input any arbitrary category value.
bugs.suggested_fix: Implement category validation using a predefined enum or database lookup before allowing expense creation.

bugs.description: No user scoping implemented. The endpoints do not associate expenses with the authenticated user, allowing potential access to other users' data.
bugs.suggested_fix: Extract user ID from JWT token and filter all expense queries by user_id.

bugs.description: Missing input validation for amount and date fields. Invalid or malicious data can be submitted.
bugs.suggested_fix: Add Pydantic model validation to ensure amount is positive numeric and date is in valid format.

bugs.description: No pagination or time range filtering in report endpoints. This will cause performance issues with large datasets.
bugs.suggested_fix: Add optional query parameters for date range and implement pagination where appropriate.

test_cases.description: Verify that a new user can register with valid email and password
Verify that a registered user can log in and receive a token
Verify that authenticated user can create an expense with valid data
Verify that user can retrieve their own expenses
Verify that expense creation fails when category is not in predefined list

recommendations: Implement proper password hashing using bcrypt before storing in database
Secure JWT token delivery using httpOnly cookies with proper security attributes
Enforce user scoping on all expense operations to prevent data leakage
Validate all input data including category against predefined list
Add comprehensive error handling and appropriate HTTP status codes
Implement pagination and filtering for report endpoints
